findings.title: config.md undercounts the package-specific config values by one
locations: docs/src/guide/config.md:17 — "Five values vary by package and are substituted into the rendered policy: `rubric.leading_identity`, `notation.vectors`, `docs.admonition_titles`, `notation.mathbf_allowed` ... and `instruments.check-docs.argcov_policy`"
findings.description: The page lists five per-package config values, omitting `rubric.signature_types` (RULE.DOC.SIGNATURE_MIRROR's variation point: `names` vs `mirror`, schema/config.schema.json:288-296). The rendered policy this same package ships (.gbg/policy/00-index.md, imported into every consumer's CLAUDE.md) states there are SIX: "the leading identity of a docstring, how much of the method a signature repeats, the vector notation, the admonition-title rule, the admitted `\mathbf` strings and the tier RULE.DOC.ARGCOV binds at." config.md's own count and list are stale against both the schema and the tool's own policy text — a RULE.DOC.CURRENT violation (a summary naming only a subset of the current set is stale even where each item named is literally true).
findings.resolution_hint: Change "Five values" to "Six values" and add `rubric.signature_types` (with its `names`/`mirror` enum) to the list in docs/src/guide/config.md:17-21, in the same position 00-index.md gives it (second, after leading_identity).

findings.title: "consumer" is used repeatedly across the pages surface without ever being defined or @ref-linked
locations: docs/src/guide/install.md:6 — "fetches into the consumer's `docs/` environment" (first use in the site's own nav order: Home → Install → …)
docs/src/guide/config.md:6 — "`.gbg/config.toml` is the one config file of a consumer"
docs/src/guide/ledger.md:6 — "the one place a consumer records a waiver"
docs/src/guide/rounds.md:6 — "one run of one instrument over one consumer"
findings.description: "Consumer" is one of this package's own named terms of art (consumer; instrument; round; lane; hat; anchor; gate; pin; managed file; ledger), and RULE.DOC.TERMS_DEFINED requires a term of art be defined in a clause or @ref-linked at its first use, cold-read tested. Contrast with "ledger", "round", "lane" and "instrument", each of which the pages surface either defines in a clause at first use or @ref-links (e.g. index.md:16 `[ledger](@ref ledger)`) before using it bare elsewhere. "Consumer" gets neither: docs/src/index.md never uses the word at all (it describes the concept without naming it), and install.md — the first guide page in the site's own nav order (docs/make.jl:70) — introduces the bare word with no gloss and no link to a page that defines it (there is no dedicated "consumer" page or @id anchor on the pages surface). A reader who has not already absorbed index.md's unlabelled paraphrase has no way to resolve the term from the pages surface alone.
findings.resolution_hint: Either add a one-clause gloss at install.md's first use ("the consumer — the package that pins the tool —"), or give the term an @id anchor at its first mention and @ref-link every later bare use across install.md/config.md/ledger.md/rounds.md, the way "ledger" and "round" already are.
